subject: New York this week: a ninth Rikers death, a juvenile detention audit, and the Ulrich corruption trial
intro: Four new articles from Case Analytica this week, and five stories from other New York newsrooms worth your time.

items.title: Ninth Detainee Dies on Rikers Island So Far This Year
items.summary: A 36-year-old man awaiting trial on an attempted murder charge was found dead in his bed at the Davoren Center, the ninth death in city jail custody this year. The outlet reports the cause is unknown and the Department of Correction says it will investigate with city and state authorities.

items.title: NYC Juvenile Lockups Packed Beyond Capacity as Overtime Soars: Audit
items.summary: A state audit found the city's two juvenile detention centers are far over capacity, with staff overtime up fourfold and average stays nearly doubled. The number of probation officers fell by a third between 2020 and 2026, according to the 69-page report.

items.title: ICE subpoena puts a spotlight on the last emergency migrant shelter in NYC
items.summary: A federal judge ruled the city must give ICE the names and birthdates of South Bronx migrant shelter residents with “serious criminal histories,” meaning charges for any of eight listed crimes. The mayor's office says it is evaluating next steps.

items.title: Top NYC mayoral aide cast shadow over first Adams-era corruption trial
items.summary: In the fourth week of Eric Ulrich's Manhattan trial, recorded calls keep mentioning Ingrid Lewis-Martin, a former chief adviser to Mayor Adams. She has not been charged in his case and has pleaded not guilty in a separate corruption case.

items.title: Former NYPD detective among four cuffed for drug sale in Manhattan and Staten Island
items.summary: The Special Narcotics Prosecutor says a wiretap investigation that began in May led to four arrests, including former NYPD detective Philip Pietrunti, whose Staten Island home held 13 unlicensed firearms. The four are accused of conspiring to sell narcotics.

ours_week.title: New York Counted 9 Deaths at Rikers and 149 in State Prisons This Year. The State's List Names Them and Gives No Cause.
ours_week.excerpt: Nine deaths in NYC jail custody and 149 on the state prison list so far in 2026, and what the Parole Board's numbers say about who goes home.
ours_week.credit: Photo: Cdogsimmons, Wikimedia Commons, public domain

ours_week.title: The Clean Slate Fix for a Missed Sealing Is a Form. The Form Doesn't Exist Yet.
ours_week.excerpt: CPL 160.57 promises sealing within 30 days of a valid form. The court system says the form will come no later than November 16, 2027, and is not available now.
ours_week.credit: Photo: Kidfly182, Wikimedia Commons, CC BY 4.0

ours_week.title: Just Released From Prison on Parole? Ask Whether a Certificate of Relief Was Issued
ours_week.excerpt: DOCCS prepares a Certificate of Relief from Disabilities for eligible people before release and sends the original to the parole office. Not everyone gets one, and the directive has no step that tells you. One account shows what happens when you ask.

ours_week.title: New York Counts Every Person in Its Jails Each Morning. I Cannot Find a Count of the Records It Has Sealed.
ours_week.excerpt: New York City reported 6,665 people in its jails today. The state has until November 16, 2027 to seal eligible convictions under the Clean Slate Act, and Case Analytica found no published count of how many it has sealed. A records request is pending.
